# Selected definition for the Cohort

Include records satisfying both:

- `ipd_cofirmado == "SI"`
- `ipd_descartado == "NO"`

For individuals with multiple qualifying records, select the
**earliest confirmed, non-discarded case-creation record**.

Only AFTER selecting one record per individual, apply:

- Calendar year: 2005–2023, inclusive
- Age at case creation: 15–65 years, inclusive

We do not substitute later records when the earliest qualifying
record falls outside these restrictions.

## Questions

1. Can we reproduce the previously reported Option B counts?
2. How many individuals are excluded by the year restriction?
3. How many are excluded by the age restriction?
4. How many fail both restrictions?
5. How many remain in the final cohort?
6. Does every included individual have exactly one record,
   representing their earliest confirmed, non-discarded entry?

**Option B is the selected working definition.**

Previously reported Option B attrition:

- 22,471 unique individuals before restrictions
- 20,388 unique individuals after restrictions
- 2,083 excluded individuals

# New analysis

## 1. Setup

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = TRUE
)

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(readxl)
library(knitr)
```

## 2. Import data and master codebook

```{r import-data}
# ============================================================
# FILE PATHS — UPDATE THESE BEFORE RUNNING ON THE REAL DATA
# ============================================================
#
# The paths below are relative to Sofia's Dissertation-Aim-1
# project folder. When running this file on another computer,
# replace BOTH paths below with the locations of:
#   1. the real registry dataset
#   2. the master codebook
#

# ---- UPDATE PATH 1: DATASET ----
data_file <- "data/raw/synthetic_data.csv"

# ---- UPDATE PATH 2: MASTER CODEBOOK ----
codebook_file <- "Dissertation_Aim1_Master_Codebook.xlsx"


# ============================================================
# IMPORT DATA AND CODEBOOK — NO PATH CHANGES NEEDED BELOW HERE
# ============================================================

dat <- read_csv(data_file)

region_codes  <- read_excel(codebook_file, sheet = "Region Codes")
comuna_codes  <- read_excel(codebook_file, sheet = "Comuna Codes")
closure_codes <- read_excel(codebook_file, sheet = "Closure Codes")
country_codes <- read_excel(codebook_file, sheet = "Country Codes")
```

## 3. Prepare and validate registry variables

```{r prepare-data}
required <- c(
  "id_persona",
  "fecha_creacion_caso",
  "edad_ano_creacion_caso",
  "ipd_cofirmado",
  "ipd_descartado"
)

missing_columns <- setdiff(required, names(dat))

if (length(missing_columns) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Required variables missing: ",
    paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

records <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    source_row = row_number(),

    creation_date = as.Date(
      parse_date(
        as.character(fecha_creacion_caso),
        format = "%d%b%Y",
        locale = locale("en")
      )
    ),

    creation_year = year(creation_date),

    age_at_creation = suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(edad_ano_creacion_caso)
    ),

    confirmed = toupper(
      trimws(as.character(ipd_cofirmado))
    ),

    discarded = toupper(
      trimws(as.character(ipd_descartado))
    ),

    option_b = !is.na(confirmed) &
      !is.na(discarded) &
      confirmed == "SI" &
      discarded == "NO"
  )

# The real-data benchmark assumes complete person IDs.
# Report missing IDs explicitly rather than silently removing
# records from the starting population.

id_check <- tibble(
  Measure = c(
    "Total records",
    "Records with missing person ID",
    "Records with unparsed creation date",
    "Records with missing age"
  ),

  N = c(
    nrow(records),
    sum(is.na(records$id_persona)),
    sum(is.na(records$creation_date)),
    sum(is.na(records$age_at_creation))
  )
)

kable(id_check)
```

## 4. Verify the fixed registry benchmarks

```{r verify-registry}
person_counts <- records %>%
  filter(!is.na(id_persona)) %>%
  count(id_persona, name = "n_records")

benchmarks <- tibble(
  Measure = c(
    "Total records",
    "Unique individuals",
    "Individuals with exactly one record",
    "Individuals with multiple records",
    "Records among individuals with multiple records",
    "Maximum records per person",
    "Confirmed SI / discarded NO records",
    "Confirmed SI / discarded SI records",
    "Confirmed NO / discarded NO records",
    "Confirmed NO / discarded SI records",
    "Missing confirmation",
    "Missing discard",
    "Missing age",
    "Missing/unparsed creation date",
    "Records younger than 15",
    "Records older than 65",
    "Records before 2005"
  ),

  Expected = c(
    53611, 49839, 46447, 3392, 7164, 9,
    23017, 0, 15789, 14805,
    0, 0, 0, 0, 4203, 1860, 1751
  ),

  Observed = c(
    nrow(records),
    nrow(person_counts),
    sum(person_counts$n_records == 1),
    sum(person_counts$n_records > 1),
    sum(person_counts$n_records[
      person_counts$n_records > 1
    ]),
    max(person_counts$n_records),

    sum(
      records$confirmed == "SI" &
        records$discarded == "NO",
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    sum(
      records$confirmed == "SI" &
        records$discarded == "SI",
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    sum(
      records$confirmed == "NO" &
        records$discarded == "NO",
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    sum(
      records$confirmed == "NO" &
        records$discarded == "SI",
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    sum(is.na(records$confirmed)),
    sum(is.na(records$discarded)),
    sum(is.na(records$age_at_creation)),
    sum(is.na(records$creation_date)),
    sum(records$age_at_creation < 15, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(records$age_at_creation > 65, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(records$creation_year < 2005, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
) %>%
  mutate(
    Match = if_else(
      Expected == Observed,
      "YES",
      "NO — REVIEW"
    )
  )

kable(
  benchmarks,
  caption = "Fixed registry benchmarks versus current run"
)

if (any(benchmarks$Match != "YES")) {
  warning(
    "Registry benchmarks do not all match. Check the data
     version and variable processing before interpretation."
  )
}
```

## 5. Final Option B cohort and exclusions

We select each individual's earliest confirmed, non-discarded
record before applying the study restrictions.

The purpose is to identify how many individuals are excluded
because of the calendar-year restriction (2005–2023), the
age restriction (15–65), or both.

```{r cohort-exclusions}
# Check for confirmed individuals with no usable creation date.

missing_date_people <- records %>%
  filter(!is.na(id_persona), option_b) %>%
  group_by(id_persona) %>%
  summarise(
    all_dates_missing = all(is.na(creation_date)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  summarise(N = sum(all_dates_missing))

knitr::kable(
  missing_date_people,
  caption = "Confirmed individuals with no usable creation date"
)

if (missing_date_people$N > 0) {
  warning("Some confirmed individuals have no usable creation date.")
}

# Select earliest confirmed, non-discarded record per person.

earliest_b <- records %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(id_persona),
    option_b,
    !is.na(creation_date)
  ) %>%
  arrange(id_persona, creation_date, source_row) %>%
  group_by(id_persona) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup()

# Determine eligibility based on the selected record.

cohort_check <- earliest_b %>%
  mutate(
    year_excluded = !between(creation_year, 2005, 2023),
    age_excluded = is.na(age_at_creation) |
      !between(age_at_creation, 15, 65),

    exclusion_reason = case_when(
      !year_excluded & !age_excluded ~ "Included",
      year_excluded & age_excluded ~ "Both year and age",
      year_excluded ~ "Year only",
      age_excluded ~ "Age only"
    )
  )

# Cohort counts.

cohort_summary <- cohort_check %>%
  count(exclusion_reason, name = "N")

knitr::kable(
  cohort_summary,
  caption = "Option B cohort inclusion and exclusion"
)

# Confirm previously reported numbers.

n_initial <- nrow(earliest_b)

n_final <- sum(cohort_check$exclusion_reason == "Included")

stopifnot(
  nrow(earliest_b) == n_distinct(earliest_b$id_persona)
)

if (n_initial != 22471 || n_final != 20388) {
  warning("Cohort counts differ from previous HTML reports.")
}
```

## 6. Detailed breakdown of excluded individuals

This table identifies whether excluded individuals fall
outside the study calendar years, below age 15, above age 65,
or fail both year and age restrictions.

Each individual is counted once.

```{r detailed-exclusions}
exclusion_table <- cohort_check %>%
  mutate(
    Reason = case_when(
      exclusion_reason == "Included" ~ "Included",

      year_excluded & age_at_creation < 15 ~
        "Year restriction and age below 15",

      year_excluded & age_at_creation > 65 ~
        "Year restriction and age above 65",

      year_excluded & is.na(age_at_creation) ~
        "Year restriction and missing age",

      year_excluded ~
        "Year restriction only",

      age_at_creation < 15 ~
        "Age below 15 only",

      age_at_creation > 65 ~
        "Age above 65 only",

      is.na(age_at_creation) ~
        "Missing age",

      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  ) %>%
  count(Reason, name = "N")

# Confirm every selected individual appears in exactly one category.

stopifnot(
  sum(exclusion_table$N) == nrow(cohort_check)
)

# Confirm the expected number of exclusions.

n_excluded <- sum(
  cohort_check$exclusion_reason != "Included"
)

if (n_excluded != 2083) {
  warning("Exclusion count differs from previous HTML report.")
}

knitr::kable(
  exclusion_table,
  caption = "Detailed Option B cohort attrition"
)
```
